title: Stoker plugins — version
description: `plugins/<key>/<version>.yaml` in a plugin registry: one version of a plugin — immutable once published, as a new binary is a new version. It may gain files for further platforms later, never change one: a file listed here is the file every host that approved this version runs. The files are the assets of the version's release on the plugin's own repository (`release`); their hashes pin the bytes, and the publisher's `signature` vouches for them.

kind.description: Repeated from `plugin.yaml`, so this file can be checked on its own.

name.description: The version's own name, when its manifest gives one other than the plugin's.

release.description: The release on the plugin's repository whose assets are this version's files. Its tag is `v<version>` in a repository of one plugin (`v1.2.0`) and `<key>/<version>` in a repository of several (`app.stokerhq.peacock/1.2.0`), so a release always says which plugin it is.

repository.description: The repository's web address: `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>`, a Forgejo one alike.

source.description: The exact source the files were built from, so every published binary says where its code is — which a copyleft licence asks of anybody passing the binary on.

signature.description: The publisher's signature on this version: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the version's statement, as IEEE P1363 (r and s, 32 bytes each), base64 — the scheme Stoker's launcher releases are signed with. The statement is UTF-8 text, every line ending in a line feed (`\n`): `stoker-plugin-v1`, the key, the version and the kind, one per line, then one line per file — `<os>\t<architecture>\t<fileName>\t<size>\t<sha256>\t<blake3>` with the size in decimal and both hashes in lowercase hex — ordered ordinally by `<os>\t<architecture>\t<fileName>`. What is signed is the files' identity, not where they are: a release moved to another host, or a mirror, still verifies.

publisher.description: The publisher's `id` in the registry's `registry.yaml`, whose key verifies the signature and whose namespaces must include this key.

value.description: Base64 of the 64-byte IEEE P1363 signature.

abi.description: Hook plugins: the hook ABI the plugin was built for, from its manifest.

hosts.description: Hook plugins: the bootstraps that may load it, from its manifest. Absent: every bootstrap that takes plugins.

manifestSha256.description: Hook plugins: SHA-256 of the manifest embedded in every file of the version (`.stkmeta`). Every file carries the identical manifest, so one configuration contract is right for all of them — and a host reading a file's manifest can tell it is this version.

loader.description: Mods: the mod loader the files are for — or, for the loader itself, which loader it is.

version.description: The loader version the mod needs at least, when it needs more than the loader's first release.

integration.description: Integration packages: the store SDK the package replaces inside a game, and which of the game's files it lays itself over. A package is one zip per architecture (one `files` entry each): its bootstrap, which goes over the store's file in the game, and its implementation together, at the paths an install lays them.

replaces.description: The store's file names the package is laid over, as a game ships them: `uplay_r1_loader64.dll`, `EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll`.

server.description: Server extensions: which stokerd can load the version. A host refuses one whose extensibility API it does not speak, or whose range its own version is outside.

stokerd.description: The stokerd versions it runs on: comparators separated by spaces, all of which must hold — `>=1.4.0 <2.0.0`.

extensibilityApi.description: The `Stoker.Extensibility` API version it was built against.

config.description: What can be configured, from the plugin's manifest: the subset of JSON Schema a host renders as a form and checks every assignment's `config` against.

requires.description: Plugins this one needs beside it, at exact versions: a BepInEx plugin needs BepInEx.

files.description: One file per operating system and architecture.

retired.description: Withdrawn: not to be chosen for anything new, and a host warns where it is assigned. What already names it keeps working and the version stays listed — an assignment is pinned, a recipe pinned to it must still resolve, and pulling a version out from under either would change an install nobody touched. A mistake is a new version plus this.

allOf.description: Managed code is one file for every architecture.
Nothing configures what is never assigned to a game or set up by an administrator: a library is loaded by other plugins, an unpacker by the ingest.

architecture.description: `il` for a pure .NET assembly, which runs on any architecture; listed once, under the operating system it was published for.

sha256.description: What a download — from the release, a mirror, or an administrator's own copy — is checked against.

blake3.description: The same file by BLAKE3, which a host's chunk store already computes for whatever it holds.

url.description: The release asset. When it is gone, the registry's mirrors (`registry.yaml`) are tried by SHA-256; the hash decides what a file is, wherever it came from.

configContract.description: Deliberately small: what the native side can honour and a generated form can show. One level of nested object, arrays of scalars only.

additionalProperties.description: Options are always closed; only `false` may be said.

labels.description: What every field may carry for the form: a title, the author's explanation shown under it, and examples — the first is the input's placeholder.

x-stoker-widget.description: How a form shows a string: as several lines, as a path, as hex bytes. There is no secret widget — the configuration is written in plain text into the game's folder.
